about: Answer A of exercise 3: one model's reply to the strong brief, unchanged, with the assistant's own notes under it.
route: a Claude Code subagent given the request text as its whole prompt; the answer saved as returned

key.reason: True: {staffFirst} promised to confirm a day by Friday (message 4) and did not (message 5). Owning it first is right.
True (message 5), and it owns the failure without an excuse.
True (message 5). The figure is written in words, so the figure check does not read it.

Two marks are defensible. On {date:msg4}, message 4 said the van comes "next week": the week this reply is written in. Written on {date:msg5}, "until next week" now means the week after: a new delay that nothing in the thread supports. Read as a repeat of message 4, it is fine. What tips it: whether the warehouse has said anything since. The second half, no confirmed day, is true.
True to the policy (rule 3), and it promises nothing.

Message 4 says {staffFirst} sent the photos and the request. The receipt, and the full request with the cash-and-carry cost, arrived only in message 5, and nothing says they were passed on. The assistant's own notes under the reply say so too. The second half, no amount and no decision today, is fine.

Two marks are defensible. The date is the assistant's own proposal and is not in the thread; its notes say so. But it promises only {staffFirst}'s own action, which the policy allows. What tips it: it is fine once {staffFirst} has decided he can keep that date, and not before. The figure check does not flag "12 March": it reads 12 as a figure, and 12 is in the thread as the cup size ({cupSize} oz).
